text: Why is a VCSEL inherently single-longitudinal-mode?
choices: Its gain medium has an unusually narrow gain bandwidth
Its very short (~1–2 μm) cavity gives a free spectral range (~50–100 THz) larger than the gain bandwidth
It uses an external fiber Bragg grating for feedback
It can only lase at cryogenic temperatures
explanation: A VCSEL's ~1–2 μm cavity makes the longitudinal-mode spacing (FSR ~50–100 THz) exceed the gain bandwidth, so only one longitudinal mode can lase. The gain bandwidth is not especially narrow, and VCSELs use monolithic DBR mirrors (R > 99%) rather than an external grating; they operate at room temperature.
